newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: PAKISTAN'S PIA BUYS ONE JET FUEL CARGO FROM KUWAIT.
newsitem.headline: PAKISTAN'S PIA BUYS ONE JET FUEL CARGO FROM KUWAIT.

text.p: Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) PIA.CN PIAA.KA has bought only one cargo of aviation jet fuel for now from Kuwait Petroleum Corp (KPC) in its 1997/1998 term contract, a PIA official said on Thursday.
The award for the remaining eight 25,000-tonne cargoes is still being evaluated, he said.
The 25,000-tonne parcel was awarded at a premium of $1.25 per barrel to MidEast spot quotes, on a cost-insurance-freight (cif) basis to Karachi, for August 15-17 delivery, the official said.
He said, state-owned KPC has agreed to sell the remaining cargoes at the same premium when PIA makes a final decision on the full award later.
The 1996/1997 contract expired on June 30, but PIA has extended it until August 31.
The tender, which closed on July 16, received up to 10 offers.

Other offers came from MidEast trader Star Energy at a premium of $1.495 per barrel, Saudi Arabia's Bakri Trading at a $1.59-premium, Swiss trader Glencore at a $1.659-premium and U.K.-based trader Hascombe at a $1.703-premium.
Traders said KPC's offer was very aggressive and was equivalent to what it would offer on its domestic market.
PIA has been buying jet fuel from KPC over the last four years.
The 1996/1997 contract was awarded at a premium of $1.45 per barrel to MidEast spot quotes, cif Karachi for 225,000 tonnes of jet fuel.
In 1995/1996, PIA took 175,000 tonnes from KPC at a $1.20-premium, cif Karachi.
